purpose: Teach: あめ/サヨナラ/ミーハー/ひとみ/られよ/スキップ/バツ/下敷き

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがあめ玉を孫に下さった
lines.en: When you were young, your father used to give candy to us grandchildren.
lines.style: Soft, steady voice like a light hand on a memory. Speaking into the past more than to the present. Unhurried, almost in a minor key.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、別れ際にサヨナラを丁寧に仰ったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and your father said goodbye so carefully at parting, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm agreement, gentle and sure. A small nod in her voice. She's adding her own memory to his, not correcting. Affectionate toward him as much as toward the memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはミーハーじゃない方だった
lines.en: Your father wasn't one for following trends, even back then.
lines.style: Still looking inward. A quiet appreciation in the tone — not pride, but recognition of something solid. Speaking softly, like he's still learning what it meant.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、優しいひとみで私を見て下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your father looked at me with such kind eyes, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: As if seeing it happen right now. Intimate but not fragile. The smallest smile audible. She's letting him witness what she witnessed — no hurry, no need to fill the silence.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「健康でいられよ」と仰った
lines.en: When you were young, your father once told me, 'Stay healthy.'
lines.style: The words come carefully, like he's quoting something sacred. Quiet pause before he speaks them. Not resigned — more like he's still holding them.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃にスキップする孫を可愛がられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And your father loved to watch the grandchildren skip and play, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: A small laugh underneath. Warm recollection. She's giving him back the image of his father delighted — a gift wrapped in a question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがバツの悪い時もあった
lines.en: There were times when your father felt embarrassed, or out of place.
lines.style: Saying something true that takes courage to admit. Slower here. Not apologizing for it — just acknowledging the fullness of the man, the moments when even he wavered.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、孫の下敷きを大事にしまわれてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your father kept the grandchildren's little notebooks so carefully, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Quieter, more intimate. The detail matters — small evidence of care that spoke volumes. Her voice holds it like he held those notebooks.
